elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about future plans, goals, and steps using going to, want, and need.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 5. Free time
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Holidays are coming
- Materials: Holiday cards, calendar, suitcase picture, COSYmanuals 'going to' page.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• express future plans with going to
• talk about wants and needs
• sequence a plan with first, then, and finally

Core Active Vocabulary (18 items):

holiday — a time when you do not work. Example: We go on holiday in July.
travel — to go to another place. Example: I want to travel to Italy.
plan — to decide what you will do. Example: We plan to visit Rome.
celebrate — to do something special for an event. Example: We celebrate her birthday.
beach — land next to the sea. Example: The children play on the beach.
ticket — a paper or digital pass for travel. Example: I bought a train ticket.
hotel — a place to sleep when travelling. Example: We stay in a small hotel.
visit — to go to see a person or place. Example: We visit our family every summer.
family — parents, children, and relatives. Example: My family is big.
going to — a future form for plans. Example: I am going to travel next month.
want to — to desire to do something. Example: I want to visit the beach.
need to — to have to do something. Example: I need to buy a ticket.
would like to — a polite way to say want to. Example: I would like to stay in a hotel.
goal — something you want to achieve. Example: My goal is to speak more English.
first — before all the others. Example: First, I wake up.
then — after that. Example: Then, I have breakfast.
finally — at the end. Example: Finally, I go to bed.
because — a word that gives a reason. Example: I want to relax because I work hard.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Holidays are coming! (talking about an upcoming event)
• I am going to travel. (future plan)
• I want to visit the beach. (expressing a want)
• I need to buy a ticket. (expressing a need)
• I would like to stay in a hotel. (polite preference)
• First, I'm going to book the ticket. Then, I'm going to pack. Finally, I'm going to travel. (sequencing a plan)
• because I want to relax. (giving a reason)

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'be going to' to talk about plans and intentions for the future.

Form:
Going to: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb. Negative: isn't / aren't going to. Question: Are you going to...?

Examples:
• I am going to travel next month.
• She is going to visit her family.
• We aren't going to stay at home.
• Are you going to come to the party?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ going to visit my family.
She ___ going to travel.
They ___ going to celebrate.
___ you going to come?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I am going to ... (travel / visit / study) ...
• She is going to ...
• We aren't going to ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What are you going to do this weekend?
• Where are you going to travel next year?
• Who are you going to visit?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your future plans with 'going to'.
• Write three sentences about a friend's future plans.
Reading: Holidays are coming

Holidays are coming! I am going to travel with my family. First, I am going to book the tickets. Then, I am going to pack. Finally, we are going to visit the beach. I want to relax because I work hard. I need to buy a new suitcase. I would like to stay in a small hotel. My sister is going to celebrate her birthday there. Are you going to travel this summer? What do you want to do?
What is the first step?
Why does the writer want to relax?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Are you going to travel this summer?
B: Yes, I am. I'm going to visit my family in Italy.
A: What do you want to do there?
B: I want to relax and see my cousins. First, I'm going to book the train. Then, I'm going to pack. Finally, I'm going to travel.
A: Do you need to buy anything?
B: Yes, I need to buy a new suitcase.
Where is the speaker going to visit?
What does the speaker need to buy?
Speaking task: Plan a holiday with your partner. Use going to, want, need, and first/then/finally.

• Are you going to travel this year?
• What do you want to do?
• What do you need to buy?
• Where would you like to stay?
• What is your goal for this year?
Role-play: You are planning a trip with a friend. Agree on the first, next, and final step, and explain why.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about a plan using going to, want/need, and first/then/finally.
Model: First, I'm going to ... Then, I need to ... Finally, I want to ...
